articles.title: Playbook - .Net MCP to keep your agents using the latest language features
articles.excerpt: I've been working on an open source project, Playbook, which is available now. The problem this solves: How it solves it: Given the same task, creating a .net 11 app both with and without the MCP, see…
articles.body: I've been working on an open source project, Playbook , which is available now. The problem this solves: .Net 11 just dropped. All AI models you can use right now were trained prior to .Net 11's release. Its possible they might have some of the early RC stuff in their training data, but unlikely any AI model you use right now will take advantage of what .net 11 gives us for a good while yet. How it solves it: This is an MCP, with information covering 491 recipes, across 24 categories (70 tagged as Blazor). This MCP allows your agent to search across the recipes to understand how things are done in your current target framework. The agent specifies which framework its interested in, and only gets back stuff relevant to its current goals and working environment.

articles.title: I built a local Gaussian splat to game-mesh converter, and sold it as a one-off instead of a subscription
articles.excerpt: Gaussian splats look amazing in a viewer. Drop one into a game engine and you hit a wall: no clean mesh, no collider, no LODs, and a file the engine can't really use. So I built Splat to Game. It take…
articles.body: Gaussian splats look amazing in a viewer. Drop one into a game engine and you hit a wall: no clean mesh, no collider, no LODs, and a file the engine can't really use. So I built Splat to Game . It takes a splat .ply (or .sog ) from Polycam, Luma, KIRI, Postshot and others, and outputs a game-ready GLB mesh with textures, a collider and 2 LODs for Unity, Unreal or Godot. Everything runs on your own PC. Your scans never leave it. How it works (short version) An Electron app drives a Python engine on your machine. On first run it downloads its AI parts (about 12 GB: PyTorch, ComfyUI and the shape models), so after that it works offline. A "Draft" takes about 8 to 13 minutes per object on an RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB.

articles.title: Why Incus, and Why I Wrote My Own Control Plane
articles.excerpt: The word "container" covers two different things. Kubernetes won the orchestration layer for application containers. Running a complete Linux system on a machine is a different line of work, and that…
articles.body: The word "container" covers two different things. Kubernetes won the orchestration layer for application containers. Running a complete Linux system on a machine is a different line of work, and that is where Incus sits. I moved the machines in my workshop to Incus. Before treating that as a matter of taste, here is how I got there, and what was still missing once I arrived. Why Incus, and not the other platforms Kubernetes is the standard for orchestrating application containers. Service discovery, rolling releases and scaling on metrics are all settled there. Its unit is the Pod, which assumes one main process that can be killed and replaced at any moment. That assumption does not fit a complete Linux system.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space .

articles.body: Explore This Section Science Citizen Science Amateur Astronomer? Be a… Overview Resources Opportunities Citizen Science Highlights About Science Activation Neutron stars are the ultra-dense, city-sized leftovers of dead stars. When they collide, they can release a brief flash of light called a kilonova . These immensely powerful events forge much of the universe’s gold, platinum and other heavy elements. Since a kilonova fades within days, astronomers have to find it fast, and no single observatory can watch the whole sky. But if you have a telescope with a camera, or access to one, you can help find and follow these cosmic fireworks as a part of NASA’s Kilonova Catcher project! Kilonova Catcher connects amateur astronomers around the world into a rapid-response network.

articles.title: NASA’s Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission Overview
articles.excerpt: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission wi…
articles.body: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft. The Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following arrival to the station, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 to grapple the spacecraft before ground controllers robotically install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading.

articles.title: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization
articles.excerpt: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network. Now, agentic AI is add…
articles.body: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network . Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers. As AI inference shifts from hyperscale training clouds—the huge centralized data centers where raw AI models ingest vast datasets and learn—to real-time, latency-sensitive applications, the need for on-premises or near-premises infrastructure grows. As a result, the gap between enterprise networks that are ready to support AI and those that are not is widening.
